records.reported_port: Yantian, Nansha and Shekou terminals, Guangdong
records.cause: Preventive closures ahead of Typhoon Ragasa
records.reported_operational_impact: WorldCargo News reported, citing market sources, that authorities preemptively closed the named Guangdong terminals on 22 September.

source.licence_notes: Redistribution terms not verified; concise attributed summary and source link only.

limitations: The report's 25 September resumption concerns a Hong Kong terminal, not the named Guangdong terminals; their reopening and backlog clearance are unverified.
A three-to-seven-day logistics delay was a forecast, not an observed shipment delay. The original OOCL update was inaccessible.
This is the same event as the linked hazard record, not an independent disruption. No case-study shipment or route has been matched.

search_window.note: The reported closure date plus a 14-day retrieval-only buffer, not a measured shutdown or recovery period.

records.reported_port: Pier G, Port of Long Beach, California
records.cause: Container collapse from the Mississippi at berth
records.reported_operational_impact: gCaptain reported that Pier G cargo operations were temporarily suspended after the collapse; by 10 September workers were unloading another vessel and trucks were moving containers. The Maritime Executive reported that Pier G was operating except in the immediate area around the Mississippi.

source.licence_notes: Redistribution terms not verified; concise attributed summary and source link only.

limitations: The resumption report is https://maritime-executive.com/article/port-of-long-beach-resumes-operations-after-container-collapse. Continued exclusion around the vessel and recovery work mean resumption did not establish complete recovery.
Other terminals were not reported affected; the precise suspension duration and specific shipment delays are unknown.
The NTSB's preliminary investigation at https://www-s.ntsb.gov/investigations/Pages/DCA25FM058.aspx reports later container counts that differ from early news estimates.
No affected case-study shipment or route has been matched.

search_window.note: The incident date plus a 14-day retrieval-only buffer; this does not assert continuous closure or recovery.

source.licence_notes: Redistribution terms not verified; concise attributed summary and source link only.

limitations: The article was updated after publication; the exact times of port suspension and resumption are not specified.
Port resumption does not establish cargo recovery, shipment delay, or the impact on the vessel and its cargo.
This is the same incident as the linked vessel record, not an independent disruption. No case-study shipment or route has been matched.

search_window.note: The explosion date plus a 14-day retrieval-only buffer, not a verified closure duration or recovery estimate.

records.reported_operational_impact: The terminal's 8 November advisory scheduled gate closure and delivery suspension for 9 November. Its 10 November advisory announced gate and cargo delivery resumption at 19:00, with vessel movements awaiting pilot confirmation.

source.licence_notes: Redistribution terms not verified; concise attributed summary and source link only.

limitations: The resumption advisory is https://cdnweb-mmt.ictsi.com/s3fs-public/inline-files/2025-MMT-CN050-MMT%20Advisory-%20Super%20Typhoon%20Uwan-Resumption%20of%20Operation.pdf.

The notices concern this terminal only; the closure was scheduled and resumption announced, not independently confirmed. Vessel resumption, full recovery, backlog clearance and individual shipment delays are unknown.

search_window.note: Fourteen days either side of the first advisory, for retrieval only; not a verified operational duration.

records.reported_port: Maher, Elizabeth; Seagirt, Baltimore; Richmond Marine Terminal
records.reported_operational_impact: Evergreen's 26 January advisory listed gate closures scheduled for 27 January at Maher in New Jersey, Seagirt in Maryland and Richmond Marine Terminal in Virginia; other listed terminals were scheduled to open.

source.licence_notes: Redistribution terms not verified; concise attributed summary and source link only.

limitations: The advisory lists planned gate statuses subject to change, not independently confirmed closures, reopening or delays. It does not cover every terminal at these ports.
The advisory incorrectly labels Baltimore's state as MA; Seagirt is in Maryland.
The linked hazard record describes the same advisory and should not be double counted. No case-study shipment or route has been matched.

records.reported_port: Port of Kaohsiung, near piers 77 and 78
records.cause: Collision between the Zeal Lumos and Haian Opus
records.reported_operational_impact: Safety4Sea reported that containers fell into the water and authorities suspended vessel traffic in the affected area. It reported operations resuming around 12:30 after the containers were secured.

source.licence_notes: Redistribution terms not verified; concise attributed summary and source link only.

limitations: Taiwan's safety board confirms the collision at https://www.ttsb.gov.tw/english/18609/28176/49882/post; the approximate reopening time is secondary reporting and does not establish an exact suspension duration or cargo recovery.
The traffic suspension was reported in the affected area, not necessarily throughout the port. No individual shipment delay was established.
Both linked records describe the same collision; avoid double counting. No case-study shipment or route has been matched.

search_window.note: The collision date plus a 14-day retrieval-only buffer, not a measured closure or recovery period.

records.cause: Port congestion, including downstream effects from Chinese port congestion
records.reported_operational_impact: Xeneta's September 2026 scorecard reported an average Singapore vessel queue of 22 per day, up from 12, and an average vessel wait of 3.1 days, up from 1.9 days.

source.licence_notes: Redistribution terms not verified; concise attributed summary and source link only.

limitations: The reported 3.1 days is an aggregate average vessel wait, not extra delay attributable to congestion or a delay for a particular shipment.
The September scorecard is a monthly observation; it does not establish the onset, end or continuous daily congestion. Exact publication date was not verified.
No particular terminal, case-study cargo, supplier or route has been matched.

approximations.basis: No start date and no stored source.published_at. The Xeneta post is dated 12 October 2026 (checked 2026-11-15), after the study end, so this record is never in scope (plan section 5.2, rule 3).

search_window.note: September 2026 scorecard period, not proof of continuous daily impact or recovery.

records.reported_port: Yangshan and Waigaoqiao terminals, Port of Shanghai
records.cause: Typhoon Saudel (landfall in southern Zhejiang around midday on 28 August 2026)
records.reported_operational_impact: Kuehne+Nagel reported that Yangshan halted empty-container operations at 04:00 and all operations at 06:00 on 27 August, and Waigaoqiao halted empty-container operations at 14:00 on 27 August. Waigaoqiao resumed at 12:00 and Yangshan at 14:00 on 28 August; Shanghai container yards resumed at 12:00 on 28 August.

source.licence_notes: Redistribution terms not independently verified; concise attributed summary and source link only.

limitations: The advisory was first published on 26 August and updated on 27 and 28 August; times are China Standard Time as reported by a freight forwarder, not a port-authority notice.

Terminal resumption does not establish cleared backlogs or on-schedule vessel calls. The advisory reports no vessel wait times; a trade blog reported berthing queues after the storm but was not independently reviewed: https://blogs.tradlinx.com/4-31m-teu-is-waiting-to-berth-as-china-ports-recover-from-saudel/.
This is the same storm as the linked Ningbo record, not an independent event. No affected case-study shipment, vessel or booking has been matched.

search_window.note: Reported suspension and resumption dates plus a 14-day retrieval-only buffer after resumption; it does not assert continuing disruption.

records.reported_port: Manila International Container Terminal and Manila South Harbor, Manila
records.cause: Yard congestion attributed variously to a seasonal import surge from mid-December, slow withdrawal of laden boxes, truck shortages, full empty-container depots and slowdowns of the Bureau of Customs e2M system.
records.reported_operational_impact: PortCalls reported that reefer yard utilisation at MICT exceeded 100% on multiple days in the first two weeks of February 2026, with overall utilisation in the mid-80s; conditions improved in March after Bureau of Customs intervention and utilisation rose again from late April. Asian Terminals Inc. warned on 26 May of forced transfer of long-dwelling cleared boxes, and on 19 June the bureau set 75% as the normal operating level.

source.licence_notes: Redistribution terms not independently verified; concise attributed summary and source link only.

limitations: The article is part 1 of a series and reports no dwell-time figures or vessel waiting times; congestion causes are contested between terminals, importers, brokers and shipping lines.
Event dates are null: the condition has no reported start or end. The search window spans the reported figures from February to the 19 June measures and is not an observed congestion interval.
The source was published after the reported period, so under the no-look-ahead rule it is a late report, known only from 2026-07-02.
Manila is an export port for Philippine case-study suppliers, but no affected shipment has been matched; import-side yard utilisation does not establish export delays.

search_window.note: February 2026 expanded to its first day through the 19 June 2026 customs measures, for retrieval only; not a verified congestion interval.

records.reported_port: Port Newark and Elizabeth container terminals, Port of New York and New Jersey
records.cause: Blizzard (13 inches of snow at Port Newark by 9 a.m. ET on 23 February 2026)
records.reported_operational_impact: FreightWaves reported that container and ro-ro operations stopped on 23 February, with gates closed at APM Terminals, Port Newark Container Terminal, Maher Terminals, Ports America and Port Liberty, and chassis depots shut. APM Terminals Elizabeth said its gates and vessel operations would reopen at 8 a.m. on 26 February, with the Port Newark depot still closed that day.

source.licence_notes: Redistribution terms not independently verified; concise attributed summary and source link only.

limitations: event_end is APM Terminals Elizabeth's announced reopening: https://www.apmterminals.com/en/port-elizabeth/practical-information/news-and-alerts/2026/260225-Operations-Update-Blizzard-Update. Other terminals' reopening times were not reviewed, and a planned modified gate on 28 February indicates backlog recovery continued.
This is a different storm from the January 2026 winter-storm record (PORT-2026-US-WINTER-001).
Newark is an entry port for case-study shipments, but no affected shipment has been matched.

search_window.note: Closure to announced reopening plus a 14-day retrieval-only buffer; it does not assert continuing closure.
